## Taxonomy and status rules

| Classification | Owner’s meaning |
| --- | --- |
| A(i) | Development: slow line detector |
| A(ii) | Development: next-generation detector |
| A(iii) | Development: detector built on the small detector |
| B(a) | Training-data creation: Google OCR / Document AI pages |
| B(b) | Training-data creation: segmenter-based correction and filtering tools |
| B(c) | Training-data creation: exact orchestration pipeline |
| B(d) | Revision pipeline: review sheets, artifacts, human publication |
| shared infrastructure | Deploy, ops, verify, types, CLI, vendor and repository governance |
| obsolete | Explicitly retired material only |
| unsure | Insufficient evidence, mixed container or unresolved boundary |

The current brief’s A(ii)/A(iii) labels are not silently equated to the older generation numbers. `docs/LINE_SEGMENTATION.md` and `research/round8/MODEL_GENERATIONS.md` describe generation 1 as the explicit slow model, generation 2 as the small neural detector plus heuristics, and generation 3 as revision of that same fast stack. Fast-line rows carry both A(ii), A(iii) and `unsure` where the current boundary is unresolved. Harvest source/corpus records that are not the exact line pipeline also retain `unsure` with B(c). Mixed containers can be `unsure`.

Status is a conservative inventory interpretation: **18 CURRENT**, **1391 RECORD**, **4 SUPERSEDED**, **28 SCRATCH**. CURRENT means a guide/contract at its named source, not proof of production qualification. RECORD preserves briefs, reports, plans, failures and snapshots without assuming they are obsolete. SUPERSEDED names an evidenced replacement. SCRATCH is reserved for explicitly local/unpublished or synthetic material. These are not deletion instructions.

## Measurement method and limits

Native `du -sh` and `du -k -d 2` measured allocation, while `git ls-files` separated index paths from other files. `git status --porcelain --ignored -uall` supplied untracked/ignored and working-tree state. Per-file `stat` supplied logical bytes and allocated blocks (512-byte units), aggregated to the same directory depths. Git index flags distinguish sparse omissions. `rg`, `head` and read-only Git commands supplied document metadata and history. No repository script, test suite, import, OCR/model job, network connection, Git mutation, deletion, move or commit was performed.

Allocation is a per-worktree/path observation. Do not sum it as uniquely occupied APFS disk space: clones, hardlinks, compressed storage, symlinks, directory accounting and concurrent writers can matter. Logical file bytes, allocated file bytes, directory `du` bytes, and uncompressed Git blob bytes are different quantities. Detailed JSON stores each separately. The snapshot is non-atomic; other inventory runs are writing their own files. These two outputs were not present during the main size scan.

Document purposes are distilled from the first 40 lines. The first ATX heading is recorded; heading-free files are explicitly unknown. Dates are the first recognized ISO or English day/month mention anywhere in the file, otherwise a date in its path. A date can describe an input or an older event; it is not asserted to be the document’s issue date. Index blob variants do not imply that dirty working-copy bytes were hashed. Supersession and production authority were not exhaustively audited.

## Bulk artifact directories and tracking

The following groups locate PNGs, JSONL.gz, HTML, crop-named paths, montage/contact-sheet-named paths and pytest XML. Name groups overlap extensions: these counts are not additive. HTML means an HTML candidate artifact, not proof every HTML file is an owner sheet. Crop/montage detection is path-based; JPEG crops without a crop-named path may not be included. Tracked counts are indexed paths, including sparse files absent locally. Allocated size comes from the corresponding complete directory map above.

## Unresolved facts and boundaries

- Original introducing branch is not encoded by Git; containing current branches do not prove branch of authorship.
- All reachable refs were used for largest blobs, not only current HEADs; repeated paths can have different historical blobs.
- No document, branch, artifact, or worktree is a deletion recommendation.
- The older detector generation numbering in LINE_SEGMENTATION.md differs from the owner taxonomy; A(ii)/A(iii) fast-line assignments retain unsure.
- Present code means static path/function/asset inspection only; no suite, rendering, import, or cloud/publication validation.
- sol/source-inventory already contains 1,825 tracked deletions; eight other worktrees omit tracked files with skip-worktree flags. These are distinct states.
- Classification and document CURRENT labels are inventory judgments; owner acceptance, correctness, physical OCR performance and generalization remain separate.
- Historical reports that say tests passed or a job/publish completed were not rerun or verified remotely.
- Supersession is reported only where a replacement is explicit; the remaining record set has not been certified as required or disposable.
- This run writes only INVENTORY_DOCS.md and docs.json in the authorized inventory directory. No commit was made.
